## Statement refuted

Equality of two smooth one-component molar Gibbs branches near a coexistence point always defines a unique differentiable pressure graph $p=p(T)$ on an open temperature interval, with slope $\Delta s/\Delta v$, even when the molar-volume jump $\Delta v$ vanishes.

## Example

Fix $T_0>0$, $p_0>0$, $g_0\in\mathbb R$, $v_0,c,\kappa>0$, and distinct positive molar entropies $s_\alpha,s_\beta$. Use units $g_0\in\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}}$, $v_0\in\mathrm{m^3\,mol^{-1}}$, $c\in\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}K^{-1}}$, and $\kappa\in\mathrm{m^3\,mol^{-1}Pa^{-1}}$. On a common open chart define
$$
g_i(T,p)=g_0-s_i(T-T_0)-\frac{c}{2T_0}(T-T_0)^2+v_0(p-p_0)-\frac{\kappa}{2}(p-p_0)^2,
$$
with $i\in\{\alpha,\beta\}$. Let $G_i=n_i g_i$ and adopt $S_i=-\partial_TG_i$, $V_i=\partial_pG_i$, $\mu_i=\partial_{n_i}G_i$, and $U_i=G_i+TS_i-pV_i$. This gives same-tag scaling and smooth local Gibbs charts. At $(T_0,p_0)$ the molar Gibbs values agree and the molar-volume jump is zero; the entropies differ.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The two smooth branch Gibbs functions and conjugate assignments above, with $\Delta s=s_\beta-s_\alpha\ne0$.

[A1] Constructed local Gibbs model: The branch functions and natural conjugates are exactly those declared in the Example; no stable-endpoint or material-preparation claim is made.

[F1] [[pthm-td-clapeyron-local]]: The local coexistence graph and slope conclusions require $\Delta v\ne0$.

[L1] [[thm-euclidean-inverse-function-theorem]]: A C1 map between open Euclidean neighborhoods with invertible derivative at a point has a local C1 inverse.

## Counterexample

1.1 At $(T_0,p_0)$, differentiation gives $S_i/n_i=s_i$, $V_i/n_i=v_0$, and $\mu_i=g_i=g_0$. Also $U_{i,T}=n_i c$, $V_{i,p}=-n_i\kappa$, and $V_{i,T}=0$, so the derivative determinant for $(T,p)\mapsto(U_i,V_i)$ at fixed positive amount is $-n_i^2c\kappa\ne0$. Thus [L1] supplies valid local state charts. The branch equality function is
$$
F(T,p):=g_\beta-g_\alpha=-(s_\beta-s_\alpha)(T-T_0),
$$
whose zero set is $T=T_0$ with every nearby chart pressure permitted. [given, A1, L1, algebra]

2.1 Here $\Delta v=v_\beta-v_\alpha=0$, so the zero set is not the graph of a unique pressure as a function of temperature on an open interval about $T_0$, and the quotient $\Delta s/\Delta v$ is undefined. The nonzero-jump hypothesis of [F1] fails, so this model does not contradict that theorem. [given, F1, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

## Example

Fix $T_0=300\,\mathrm K$, $p_0=10^5\,\mathrm{Pa}$, $g_0=1\,\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}}$, $c>0$ in $\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}K^{-1}}$, and $\kappa>0$ in $\mathrm{m^3\,mol^{-1}Pa^{-1}}$. On a common open chart define
$$
g_i(T,p)=g_0-s_i(T-T_0)-\frac{c}{2T_0}(T-T_0)^2+v_i(p-p_0)-\frac{\kappa}{2}(p-p_0)^2,
$$
for $i\in\{\alpha,\beta\}$, with $s_\alpha=2\,\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}K^{-1}}$, $s_\beta=5\,\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}K^{-1}}$, $v_\alpha=1.0\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{m^3\,mol^{-1}}$, and $v_\beta=4.0\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{m^3\,mol^{-1}}$. Set $G_i=n_i g_i$ and use the natural Gibbs assignments $S_i=-\partial_TG_i$, $V_i=\partial_pG_i$, $\mu_i=\partial_{n_i}G_i$, and $U_i=G_i+TS_i-pV_i$. Thus same-tag homogeneity is explicit. Assume the constructed model stipulates an attained coexistence endpoint with energy, volume, and species pairwise transfer curves feasible for all sufficiently small increments of either sign while every nonselected phase and auxiliary coordinate is fixed, and a reversible $\alpha\to\beta$ conversion in contact with an ideal thermal reservoir at $T_0$. The reversible conversion is a record of the complete finite isolated compound comprising converted phases, the fixed-temperature reservoir, work stores and all auxiliaries, with equilibrium endpoints and additive component entropy. The forward and reverse complete-compound records are admitted in the core closed class of *Thermodynamic process records and transfer conventions*, each with a supplied positive total mass, defined endpoint center-of-mass velocities in its fixed Galilean chart, and zero endpoint changes of compound center-of-mass kinetic and separately tracked external-field energies. Every component other than the converted phases and reservoir has zero entropy change, and the reservoir change is $-Q/T_0$. These are the exact additional entropy premises of the local Clapeyron theorem. These parameters and endpoint assumptions are model inputs, not empirical claims.

## Example references

[[def-td-process-and-protocol]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Gibbs functions, conjugate assignments, parameter values and units, common open chart, attained exchange equilibrium, and reversible reservoir operation in the Example.

[A1] Constructed model assumptions: $G_i=n_i g_i$ on each fixed tag, the central state is an attained coexistence equilibrium with the three pure pairwise bilateral transfer curves specified above, and the phase conversion is reversible in an ideal bath at $T_0$ through the complete core closed forward and reverse compound records specified in the Example.

[F1] [[pthm-td-clapeyron-local]]: For the stated one-component C1 branches with local C2 energy representations, same-tag homogeneity, exchange equilibrium, nonzero molar-volume jump and reversible ideal-bath conversion, the local slope is $\Delta s/\Delta v$ and the absorbed molar heat is $T\Delta s$.

[L1] [[thm-euclidean-inverse-function-theorem]]: A C1 map between open Euclidean neighborhoods with invertible derivative at a point has a local C1 inverse.

[L2] [[thm-ck-euclidean-maps-closed-under-algebra-and-composition]] preserves $C^2$ under finite algebra and composition. [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]] gives $(n^{-1})'=-n^{-2}$ and $(n^{-2})'=-2n^{-3}$ for $n>0$, so the reciprocal is $C^2$ there by these continuous derivative formulas.

[L3] [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]: differential identities pull back through differentiable coordinate maps by the total-derivative chain rule.

[F2] [[post-td-macroscopic-second-law]]: on each admitted core closed isolated-compound record with the stated zero excluded-energy changes and admitted additive equilibrium endpoint split, total entropy does not decrease. For the stipulated forward and reverse records, these inequalities give zero total entropy change.

## Verification

1.1 For each branch choose a reference amount $n_i>0$ and a full open neighborhood $\mathcal O_i$ of $(T_0,p_0,n_i)$ in $(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R\times(0,\infty)$. Define $\chi_i(T,p,n)=(U_i(T,p,n),V_i(T,p,n),n)$ by the Gibbs assignments. At the center, differentiation gives $S_i/n_i=s_i$, $V_i/n_i=v_i$, and $\mu_i=g_i=g_0$. Also $U_{i,T}=n_i c$, $V_{i,p}=-n_i\kappa$, and $V_{i,T}=0$ there. The full Jacobian of $\chi_i$ is block triangular with last diagonal entry $1$, so its determinant is $-n_i^2c\kappa\ne0$. By [L1], shrink $\mathcal O_i$ to an open inverse patch retaining positive temperature, volume and amount. Its numerical state patch is $O_{c_i}=\Phi_{c_i}^{-1}(\chi_i(\mathcal O_i))$, using the SI unit map in [F1]'s phase-branch definition; define its entropy by the displayed Gibbs assignment through this inverse. Thus $\Delta s=3\,\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}K^{-1}}$ and $\Delta v=3.0\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{m^3\,mol^{-1}}\ne0$. [given, A1, F1, L1, algebra]

2.1 For entropy $\mathsf s$ near $n_i s_i$, positive amount $n$ near $n_i$, and volume $V$ near $n_i v_i$, solve the natural assignments explicitly by $T(\mathsf s,V,n)=T_0+(T_0/c)(\mathsf s/n-s_i)$ and $p(\mathsf s,V,n)=p_0+(v_i-V/n)/\kappa$. Set $\mathcal U_i(\mathsf s,V,n)=n g_i(T,p)+T\mathsf s-pV$. These maps are $C^2$ by [L2], and substitution gives $S_i=\mathsf s$, $V_i=V$, and $U_i=\mathcal U_i$. On a sufficiently small neighborhood $T,n,V$ are positive. Scaling $(\mathsf s,V,n)$ by $\lambda$ leaves both ratios unchanged, so $T,p$ are unchanged and $\mathcal U_i(\lambda\mathsf s,\lambda V,\lambda n)=\lambda\mathcal U_i(\mathsf s,V,n)$ whenever both states remain in this local patch. This explicitly supplies the required fixed-tag $C^2$ homogeneous energy representation. [given, A1, L2, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

3.1 The Gibbs assignments and [L3] give $dU_i=T\,dS_i-p\,dV_i+g_i\,dn$ on the inverse patch of step 1.1. Consequently its entropy partials are $S_{i,U}=1/T$, $S_{i,V}=p/T$, and $S_{i,n}=-g_i/T$. The inverse coordinates are $C^1$ by [L1]; the reciprocal is $C^1$ and the polynomial $g_i$ is smooth by [L2]. Hence these coefficients are $C^1$, giving $C^2$ entropy with $S_{i,U}>0$ and the intended derivative-defined intensives. Conversely the explicit formulas in step 2.1 invert the energy-to-Gibbs coordinates, so the natural-variable chart is valid. The branch maps are therefore legitimate local phase and Gibbs charts with the regularity required by [F1]. [given, A1, F1, L1, L2, L3, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 Apply the slope clause of [F1] with [A1] and the verified charts:
$$
\left.\frac{dp}{dT}\right|_{(T_0,p_0)}=\frac{\Delta s}{\Delta v}=\frac{3}{3.0\times10^{-3}}=1.0\times10^3\,\mathrm{Pa\,K^{-1}}.
$$
For the latent heat, [F2] on the specified forward and reverse complete-compound records gives zero total entropy change. All components except the phases and reservoir have zero entropy change, and the latter contributes $-Q/T_0$, so conversion of $n>0$ moles gives $0=n\Delta s-Q/T_0$. Thus $\ell_{\alpha\to\beta}:=Q/n=T_0\Delta s=300(3)=900\,\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}}$, also the latent-heat formula of [F1]. Both values are exact constructed-model predictions under the stated preparation assumptions. [given, A1, F1, F2, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Let $\alpha,\beta$ be two one-component phase branches from *Phase branches and coexistence domains* on a common open chart $O\subset(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$ with coordinates $(T,p)$. Assume each branch has a local $C^2$ energy representation $\mathcal U_i(s,V,n)$, $i\in\{\alpha,\beta\}$, and that within each fixed branch tag it satisfies the same-tag homogeneity
$$
\mathcal U_i(\lambda s,\lambda V,\lambda n)=\lambda\mathcal U_i(s,V,n)
$$
for all $\lambda$ in a neighborhood of $1$ for which the scaled state remains in the chart. This is a phase-branch hypothesis: the general tagged law of *Additive separated systems and tagged bulk scaling* does not imply it. It may be stipulated independently on each local branch, or supplied by the common-law bulk subclass of *Euler and Gibbs-Duhem identities under same-tag homogeneity* when each phase's local inverse states lie in its designated entropy cone with fixed species and intensive parameters and common SI units and energy/entropy reference conventions. That supplied subclass uses local inverse uniqueness and does not require a global energy inverse.

Suppose a state $(T_0,p_0)\in O$ is an attained interior coexistence equilibrium with bilateral energy, volume, and species exchange between the two branches, and both branches admit the valid local Gibbs charts of *Local thermodynamic Legendre potentials*. Precisely, in each of these three exchange directions, feasible nonzero pure pairwise increments approach zero from each sign, while every nonselected coordinate of both phases, every other phase, and every auxiliary state is fixed at its endpoint value. Write $g_i=G_i/n_i$, $s_i=S_i/n_i$, and $v_i=V_i/n_i$ in the units specified by *SI quantities and unit conventions*. If
$$
\Delta v(T_0,p_0):=v_\beta(T_0,p_0)-v_\alpha(T_0,p_0)\ne0,
$$
then, on some open interval about $T_0$, the equal-Gibbs-per-mole coexistence condition $g_\alpha(T,p(T))=g_\beta(T,p(T))$ defines a unique local $C^1$ curve and
$$
\frac{dp}{dT}=\frac{s_\beta-s_\alpha}{v_\beta-v_\alpha}.
$$
If, in addition, conversion from $\alpha$ to $\beta$ is admitted as a reversible process in contact with an ideal thermal reservoir at the same fixed $T$, and the full finite isolated compound (converted phases, reservoir, work stores and all auxiliaries) has equilibrium endpoints with additive component entropy, with every component other than the converted phases and that reservoir having zero entropy change, and the admitted forward and reverse complete-compound records have nonnegative total endpoint entropy changes for that same additive split with their full endpoint tuples interchanged, then its molar latent heat absorbed by the system is $\ell_{\alpha\to\beta}=T(s_\beta-s_\alpha)$. These are conditional model deductions. The slope conclusion is not asserted when $\Delta v=0$ or where the branch charts are not $C^1$.

## Statement references

[[def-td-phase-and-coexistence-domain]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Two pure phase branches on a common open $(T,p)$ chart; positive one-component amounts; the C2 local energy and Gibbs maps and C1 phase-branch maps stated above; the same-tag homogeneity assumption for each phase; an attained interior maximum with bilateral energy, volume, and species exchange; $\Delta v(T_0,p_0)\ne0$; and, for the latent-heat clause, a reversible conversion with a fixed-temperature ideal reservoir. Use SI units: $T$ in kelvins, $p$ in pascals, $G$ in joules, $n$ in moles, $s$ in $\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}K^{-1}}$, and $v$ in $\mathrm{m^3\,mol^{-1}}$.

[A1] Each phase's fixed-tag local C2 energy representation has the degree-one homogeneity stated in the Statement. This may be an independent local constitutive hypothesis or the supplied common-law bulk subclass of [[pthm-td-euler-and-gibbs-duhem]] under its exact inverse-chart and reference conventions. The general tagged-scaling postulate alone does not supply it.

[A2] The admitted reversible conversion and its reverse are records of the complete finite isolated compound with aggregate equilibrium endpoints represented by full constituent and auxiliary state tuples. Its components include the converted phases, the ideal thermal reservoir at fixed $T$, and every work store or auxiliary, with an adopted additive total endpoint entropy map $S_{\mathrm{tot}}$. Each other component has zero endpoint entropy change, and the reservoir contributes $-Q/T$ when heat $Q$ is absorbed by the system. The reverse record interchanges the two full endpoint tuples and reverses the signed transfer, as required by [[def-td-reversible-process]]. Adopt explicitly $\Delta S_{\mathrm{tot}}[P]\ge0$ and $\Delta S_{\mathrm{tot}}[P^{\mathrm{rev}}]\ge0$ for these two records. Since their entropy changes are negatives, $\Delta S_{\mathrm{tot}}[P]=0$. The postulate [[post-td-macroscopic-second-law]] supplies these inequalities when its admitted core-record, complete endpoint-association and additive-split hypotheses hold; without that additional discharge, the two inequalities are separate adopted model premises of this latent-heat clause. No entropy premise is needed for the slope-only clause.

[F1] [[def-td-phase-and-coexistence-domain]]: a one-component branch supplies $g=G/n$, $s=S/n$, and $v=V/n$ on its valid positive-temperature chart; the definition does not assert $g=\mu$ without same-tag homogeneity.

[F2] [[def-td-legendre-potentials]]: on its valid local natural-variable chart, $G=U-Ts+pV$.

[F3] [[pthm-td-intensive-coexistence-conditions]]: at an attained entropy maximum, pure pairwise energy, volume, and species transfers with feasible nonzero increments approaching zero from each sign, and every nonselected phase and auxiliary coordinate fixed, give equal positive temperatures, equal pressures, and equal chemical potentials. The Statement supplies exactly these transfer hypotheses.

[F4] [[pthm-td-potential-differentials]]: Its current carrier is published and includes verification evidence. On a valid local $C^2$ energy-representation chart with the stated natural-coordinate inverse charts, its Statement gives $dG=-S\,dT+V\,dp+\sum_j\mu_j\,dn_j$. Its Proof derives this identity from the local energy conjugate identities, the Legendre-potential definitions, and the published $C^2$ partial-Legendre differential lemma; it does not assert that heat or work is an exact differential on process space.

[F5] [[pthm-td-euler-and-gibbs-duhem]]: if the same-tag homogeneity [A1] holds on a valid local C2 energy chart, its current Statement gives $U=Ts-pV+\mu n$, hence $G/n=\mu$. Its general conditional implication requires [A1], and its separately designated common-law bulk subclass derives that local premise from adopted entropy transport and local inverse uniqueness. Neither route silently equates distinct physical system tags.

[L1] [[thm-tdmath-local-implicit-rank]]: Its current mathematical carrier is published and has verification evidence. Its Statement gives a unique local $C^1$ graph of dimension $n-q$ for a $C^1$ map $F:U\subseteq\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^q$ with $F(x_*)=0$ and an invertible $q\times q$ derivative minor; when $q=n$, the zero is locally isolated. Its Proof reduces the nonsquare case by a coordinate permutation to the Euclidean implicit-function theorem and the square case to the inverse-function theorem. Here $F=g_\beta-g_\alpha$ is $C^1$ on the stated open chart and $F_p=v_\beta-v_\alpha\ne0$, so the required scalar minor is invertible.

[L2] [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]: differentiating a composition of differentiable maps gives the composed derivative.

## Proof

1.1 By [F3], bilateral energy, volume, and species exchange give common $T_0,p_0$ and $\mu_\alpha=\mu_\beta$ at the attained interior coexistence point. Apply [F5] separately to the two phase branches using [A1]: $G_i/n_i=\mu_i$ for $i=\alpha,\beta$. Thus $F(T_0,p_0):=g_\beta(T_0,p_0)-g_\alpha(T_0,p_0)=0$. [given, A1, F3, F5, algebra]

1.2 On each branch, hold the amount $n_i$ fixed while varying $(T,p)$. By [F2] and [F4], $d(G_i/n_i)=-s_i\,dT+v_i\,dp$. Consequently $F_T=-(s_\beta-s_\alpha)$ and $F_p=v_\beta-v_\alpha$ at $(T_0,p_0)$. The nonzero-volume-jump hypothesis makes $F_p\ne0$. [given, F1, F2, F4, algebra]

2.1 Apply [L1] to $F=g_\beta-g_\alpha$ on $O$. It gives a unique local C1 graph $p=p(T)$ satisfying $F(T,p(T))=0$. Differentiating this identity using [L2] gives $0=F_T+F_p\,p'(T)$. Substitution of the derivatives from step 1.2 yields
$$
p'(T_0)=\frac{s_\beta-s_\alpha}{v_\beta-v_\alpha}.
$$
The same calculation applies at every point of the shrunken coexistence interval with nonzero $\Delta v$. [L1, L2, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 For the reversible latent-heat clause, the system entropy change when $n$ moles are converted is $n(s_\beta-s_\alpha)$. By [A2], the full isolated compound has zero total entropy change; all other components have zero entropy change, and the reservoir contributes $-Q/T$, so $Q/T=n(s_\beta-s_\alpha)$. Dividing by $n>0$ gives $\ell_{\alpha\to\beta}:=Q/n=T(s_\beta-s_\alpha)$. This conclusion is conditional on the stated reversible operation and ideal reservoir; it is not a property of an arbitrary irreversible conversion path. [given, A2, F1, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

The statement's same-tag homogeneity is deliberately local to each branch. The Euler supplier preserves the general implication from independently stipulated local homogeneity and also supplies it on the separately adopted common-law bulk branch. The general tagged postulate still allows $c^{(\lambda)}\ne c$; neither constitutive route is a proof of exact extensivity for every finite body, surface-sensitive or long-range system, or gravitating system. Valid Gibbs charts, admitted bilateral exchanges, positive amounts, the nonzero molar-volume jump, and the reversible ideal-reservoir qualification remain essential.

## Remarks

The branch theorems on this page require the stated smooth local charts. Here coexistence means an attained global entropy-maximizing endpoint on the exact feasible set of *Phase branches and coexistence domains*; equality of intensive phase data follows only for the bilateral exchanges assumed in the branch theorems and does not itself imply loss of chart regularity. The smooth-branch conclusions apply only on their specified C1 charts and interior composition domains. They supply no conclusion where a branch chart fails to be C1, a species amount reaches the composition boundary, or the specified coexistence-and-affinity Jacobian lacks its required nonsingular minor. In particular, *Local Clapeyron slope on a regular pure-phase coexistence branch* requires a nonzero molar-volume jump; when that jump vanishes, its local graph argument and quotient formula do not apply.

The compact-mixture result *Attained entropy-maximizing mixtures on compact phase domains* requires a compact phase-generator domain, a continuous entropy map, a fixed barycenter, and feasibility of all probability mixtures with that barycenter. It supplies no attainment theorem for noncompact domains. Likewise, *Finite-state thermodynamic-limit contract* specifies the sequence and normalization for a limiting claim but proves no limit exists and no derivatives commute with that limit.

A finite-state partition sum is finite and positive at each finite system size. A singular phase behavior therefore needs a separately specified limit or another model with a separately established domain and regularity analysis. This page does not assert a universal thermodynamic-limit theorem, ensemble equivalence, critical exponent, or physical applicability of the van der Waals equation.

The local homogeneity used by *Local Clapeyron slope on a regular pure-phase coexistence branch* may be independently stipulated in a phase model or supplied on the separately designated common-law bulk branch under the local Euler theorem's inverse-chart and common-reference conditions. A constructed local Gibbs model need not be embedded in a global bulk cone to use the general conditional result. The added branch supplies no universal finite-size, long-range or gravitational extensivity and does not remove any smoothness, exchange or nonzero-volume-jump condition.
